title: Microsoft event debuts new AI-friendly hardware and Windows changes
content:
In its first live event in two years, Microsoft today announced its newest Surface laptop, outlined a host of changes coming to Windows 11, and shared a vision of how local-AI and agentic workflows could reshape personal computing for those in the dev community as well as home enthusiasts.
Surface Laptop Ultra
Originally teased in May 2026, the new Surface Laptop Ultra will be Microsoft’s first offering to take advantage of the new Nvidia RTX Spark SoC (system on a chip). The device has a starting price of $2,599 and comes in various SoC and memory configurations, with either a 5120-core or 6144-core Blackwell GPU and up to 128GB of LPDDR5x unified memory. It will begin shipping on October 16 and is available for preorder now.
While the new Ultra is clearly focused on the developer crowd, graphical performance was highlighted during the presentation to show off just how capable the laptop can be. By leaning on unified memory allocation rather than the physical VRAM limits of a traditional GPU, the laptop can assign its resources to handle modern gaming tasks as well as local AI development and deployment. The new Gears of War: E-Day was shown running on the system, meaning that even without a traditional gaming GPU, AAA titles are on the table.
RTX Spark Dev Box
Joined on stage by Nvidia’s Jensen Huang and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, President of Windows and Devices Pavan Davuluri also unveiled the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box. This is a $5,999 anodized aluminum black box “designed to meet the needs of frontier developers.” The Spark Dev Box ships with a custom “developer-optimized” build of Windows 11 pre-configured for AI development and local AI use. With 128GB of unified memory and the onboard Nvidia RTX GPU, the box claims one petaflop (that’s 1,000 teraflops) of AI compute performance.

report.summary: Microsoft unveiled Surface Laptop Ultra and RTX Spark Dev Box with Nvidia chips, plus Windows 11 changes aimed at local AI and agentic workflows.
report.background: Microsoft's first live event in two years arrives as PC makers race to define the AI PC era. Apple's unified-memory Macs have become popular for local LLM work, while Nvidia dominates AI accelerators but has had a smaller presence in consumer/client SoCs. Windows 11 has also faced criticism over AI features and performance, so Microsoft needs a compelling developer story. The RTX Spark SoC, built with Blackwell graphics and up to 128GB unified memory, is meant to remove VRAM bottlenecks for local AI training, inference, and gaming. By tying new Surface hardware to Windows 11 changes and agentic workflows, Microsoft is positioning Windows as a first-class platform for local AI, not just cloud services, and courting developers who want to run models on their own machines.
key_points: Surface Laptop Ultra is Microsoft's first device with Nvidia's RTX Spark SoC. It starts at $2,599, offers 5120-core or 6144-core Blackwell GPU options, up to 128GB LPDDR5x unified memory, and ships October 16 with preorders open now. Microsoft highlighted both gaming and local AI development.

The Surface RTX Spark Dev Box is a $5,999 black anodized desktop for frontier developers. Unveiled with Nvidia's Jensen Huang and Microsoft's Satya Nadella, it ships with a developer-optimized Windows 11 build, 128GB unified memory, an onboard RTX GPU, and a claimed one petaflop of AI compute.

Unified memory is central to both machines. Instead of being limited by traditional GPU VRAM, the systems allocate memory dynamically for AAA gaming, local AI development, and deployment. Microsoft showed Gears of War: E-Day running on the laptop to prove the hardware can handle graphics-intensive workloads.

Microsoft outlined a host of Windows 11 changes and a vision for local-AI and agentic workflows. The company argues these features could reshape personal computing for developers and home enthusiasts, moving AI from cloud APIs to on-device agents and models.

The event signals a deeper Microsoft-Nvidia partnership and a direct challenge to Apple Silicon's unified-memory advantage. It also raises the bar for AI PC hardware, with high prices and power demands likely limiting early adoption to professional developers and enthusiasts.
report.impact: For the AI industry, Microsoft and Nvidia's push validates local AI as a mainstream PC category, not just a cloud workload. It pressures Apple, AMD, Intel, and Qualcomm to offer more unified memory and stronger on-device inference. Developers gain machines that can run larger models, fine-tune locally, and build agentic apps without cloud latency or data-egress costs, though $2,599 to $5,999 prices may restrict access. Regular users could see more offline, privacy-preserving AI features in Windows, but also higher hardware costs, compatibility questions, and potential bloat. If Windows 11's agentic workflows mature, the PC could shift from app launcher to proactive assistant.
report.tools: Watch Nvidia CUDA, TensorRT-LLM, NVIDIA NIM, and RTX Spark developer docs for optimized local inference. On Windows, follow Windows AI Foundry, DirectML, ONNX Runtime, WSL2, and Windows Insider builds for agentic features. For trying local models, use Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, or vLLM. Microsoft's developer-optimized Windows 11 build and Surface RTX Spark Dev Box documentation will be key references.
